title: Product Co-Purchase Affinity Score
description:
Find all pairs of products that were purchased together in the same order, and count how many times each pair appears. Return each pair once (lower `product_id` first).

**Table: order_items** — `order_id`, `product_id`, `product_name`

Output columns: `product1_id`, `product1_name`, `product2_id`, `product2_name`, `co_occurrence_count`. Order by `co_occurrence_count DESC`, `product1_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, product_name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,1,'Widget A'),(1,2,'Gadget B'),(1,3,'Doohickey C'),(2,1,'Widget A'),(2,2,'Gadget B'),(3,2,'Gadget B'),(3,3,'Doohickey C'),(4,1,'Widget A'),(4,3,'Doohickey C'),(5,1,'Widget A'),(5,2,'Gadget B');
solution_sql: SELECT a.product_id AS product1_id, a.product_name AS product1_name, b.product_id AS product2_id, b.product_name AS product2_name, COUNT(*) AS co_occurrence_count FROM order_items a JOIN order_items b ON a.order_id = b.order_id AND a.product_id < b.product_id GROUP BY a.product_id, a.product_name, b.product_id, b.product_name ORDER BY co_occurrence_count DESC, product1_id;

test_cases.description: Widget A + Gadget B co-appear in orders 1,2,5 (count=3); Widget A + Doohickey C in 1,4 (count=2); Gadget B + Doohickey C in 1,3 (count=2) — 3 pairs

hints: Self-join order_items on a.order_id = b.order_id with a.product_id < b.product_id to get unique pairs per order.
Each matching row represents one co-occurrence; COUNT(*) aggregated by product pair gives the frequency.
The condition a.product_id < b.product_id prevents duplicate pairs and self-pairs.
explanation: Joining on same order_id with a.product_id < b.product_id finds all product pairs sharing an order. Pair (Widget A, Gadget B): orders 1, 2, 5 = 3 times. Pair (Widget A, Doohickey C): orders 1, 4 = 2 times. Pair (Gadget B, Doohickey C): orders 1, 3 = 2 times. These are the only 3 pairs. High co-occurrence suggests bundling opportunities.
